story.en:
Zhang Heng grew up in Nanyang and refused several early offers of office, spending ten years on his Rhapsody on the Two Capitals, a long poem contrasting the luxury of Chang'an with the restraint of Luoyang. His interest in mathematics and the heavens brought him to court, where he served twice as Grand Astrologer.

He described the cosmos as an egg, with the earth like the yolk inside a spherical heaven, and built a bronze armillary sphere turned by a water clock so that it matched the sky. His most famous device, according to the Hou Han shu, was a bronze vessel with eight dragons around its rim, each holding a ball over the open mouth of a toad. When the earth shook, a ball dropped and showed the direction. One day a ball fell with no tremor felt in Luoyang, and the court scoffed, until a messenger arrived days later reporting an earthquake in Longxi, far to the west.

No example survives, and modern reconstructions are guesses at the mechanism. Zhang Heng spent his last years fighting corruption as chancellor of Hejian and wrote poems of disillusion with court life.
story.zh:
张衡在南阳长大，早年多次辞谢征召，用十年时间写成《二京赋》，对比长安的奢华与洛阳的节俭。他精于数学和天文，被召入朝，两度出任太史令。

他主张浑天说，认为天如鸡蛋，地如蛋黄居于其中，并制作了以漏壶水力驱动的铜浑天仪，使其运转与天象相合。据《后汉书》记载，他最有名的发明是候风地动仪：铜铸，形似酒樽，外有八条龙，龙口各衔铜丸，下有蟾蜍张口承接。一旦地动，铜丸落下，便可知地震方向。有一次一颗铜丸落下，洛阳却毫无震感，朝中众人都觉得可笑，几天后驿使来报，陇西果然发生了地震。

地动仪原物早已失传，现代复原只是对其机理的推测。张衡晚年出任河间相，整治豪强，又作诗抒发对官场的失望。

Britannica: Hua Tuo

note: Birth year unknown (c. 140–145). Some of his cures in the Sanguozhi are legendary; the Romance of the Three Kingdoms story of brain surgery on Cao Cao is fiction.

story.en:
Hua Tuo declined official posts and travelled around the Huai and Si rivers as a physician. Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms collects his cases: he gave patients a powder dissolved in wine, mafeisan, until they were insensible, opened the abdomen to remove diseased parts, stitched the wound and applied ointment, and the patient recovered within a month. He told the governor Chen Deng that his stomach was full of worms from eating raw fish, gave him a decoction, and Chen vomited up three pints of them; he warned that the illness would return in three years, and it did, when Hua Tuo was not there to treat it.

He taught that the body should be exercised as a door hinge that moves does not rot, and devised the 'Five Animals Play', imitating the tiger, deer, bear, monkey and bird. His pupil Wu Pu is said to have lived past ninety with his hearing and teeth intact.

Cao Cao, who suffered from severe headaches, made him his personal physician. Hua Tuo went home, claimed his wife was ill and would not return. Cao had him arrested and killed. Before dying he offered his book to the jailer, who was too frightened to take it, and Hua Tuo burned it.
story.zh:
华佗不愿做官，在淮河、泗水一带行医。陈寿《三国志》记载了他的许多医案：遇到需要开刀的病，他让病人以酒服下"麻沸散"，待其失去知觉，剖开腹部切除病灶，再缝合伤口、敷上药膏，一个月内即可痊愈。他诊断广陵太守陈登胃中有虫，是吃生鱼所致，开汤药让陈登吐出三升多虫子；又说三年后病会复发，届时陈登果然发病，华佗却不在身边，陈登不治而死。

他认为人体应当常常活动，"户枢不朽"，并创编"五禽戏"，模仿虎、鹿、熊、猿、鸟的动作。据说他的弟子吴普依法锻炼，年过九十仍耳聪目明、牙齿完坚。

曹操患头风，召华佗为侍医。华佗告假回乡，以妻子生病为由久久不归。曹操大怒，将他下狱处死。临死前华佗拿出一卷医书交给狱吏，狱吏怕担罪责不敢接受，华佗便把书烧了。

summary.en: Born in Kucha to an Indian father and a Kuchean princess, he studied in Kashmir and Kashgar, was held for seventeen years in Liangzhou after the Former Qin took Kucha, and was brought to Chang'an by the Later Qin in 401. summary.en: Yang Yuhuan was first married to Xuanzong's son Prince Shou; the emperor took her as his favourite, and her cousin Yang Guozhong became chief minister. Blamed by the guards for the An Lushan rebellion, she was put to death at Mawei. Bai Juyi's Song of Everlasting Sorrow made her one of China's great tragic figures.

Britannica: Yang Guifei

note: Her birthplace is disputed (Shu, Yongle in Shanxi, or Huayin); the childhood stop is approximate.

story.en:
Yang Yuhuan, orphaned young and raised by an uncle, was married at about sixteen to Li Mao, Prince Shou, a son of Emperor Xuanzong. When the emperor's beloved Consort Wu died in 737 he was disconsolate, and someone pointed him to his daughter-in-law. To avoid open scandal she was first made a Daoist nun with the name Taizhen, and in 745 she was formally named Guifei, 'precious consort'.

She was a fine dancer and musician, and the court histories describe the favours heaped on her family: her three sisters were made duchesses, and her cousin Yang Guozhong rose to chief minister. Lychees were rushed by relay riders from the south so that she could eat them fresh; Du Mu later wrote of the horseman's dust that made the consort smile. An Lushan, a frontier general, cultivated her and was even adopted as her son in a palace jest.

When An Lushan rebelled in 755 and Chang'an was threatened, the emperor fled west. At Mawei the guards killed Yang Guozhong and refused to march on until she too was dead. Xuanzong had Gao Lishi strangle her in a Buddhist chapel. Bai Juyi's Song of Everlasting Sorrow (806) turned the story into romance.
story.zh:
杨玉环幼年丧父，由叔父抚养，约十六岁时嫁给唐玄宗之子寿王李瑁。737年玄宗宠爱的武惠妃去世，玄宗郁郁寡欢，有人向他推荐了这位儿媳。为了避人耳目，她先出家为女道士，号"太真"，745年正式册封为贵妃。

她善歌舞、通音律，史书记载杨氏一门因此显贵：三个姐姐分封韩国、虢国、秦国夫人，堂兄杨国忠官至宰相。岭南荔枝由驿马飞驰送到长安，让她吃上新鲜的，杜牧后来写下"一骑红尘妃子笑，无人知是荔枝来"。边将安禄山百般讨好她，甚至在宫中戏认她为母。

755年安禄山起兵，长安危急，玄宗西逃。行至马嵬驿，禁军杀死杨国忠，又以"贼本尚在"为由，不肯前行。玄宗只得命高力士将她缢死于佛堂。白居易作于806年的《长恨歌》把这段故事化作了千古传唱的爱情悲歌。

summary.en: Tang poet who wrote in plain language for ordinary readers, from social satires such as The Old Charcoal Seller to the narrative Song of Everlasting Sorrow and Pipa Song. As governor of Hangzhou he built the dyke on West Lake; he spent his last years in Luoyang.
summary.zh: 唐代诗人，作诗力求通俗，"老妪能解"。代表作有讽喻诗《卖炭翁》及长篇叙事诗《长恨歌》《琵琶行》。任杭州刺史时筑堤治理西湖，晚年退居洛阳。

label.en: Zhouzhi: writes the Song of Everlasting Sorrow
Demoted to Jiangzhou; writes the Pipa Song
Governor of Hangzhou; builds the West Lake dyke

sources.title: 刘昫等《旧唐书》卷166 白居易传

summary.en: Leader of the 'ancient prose' movement and first of the Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song, he defended Confucian orthodoxy against Buddhism and Daoism. His 819 memorial against honouring a relic of the Buddha nearly cost him his life and sent him into exile at Chaozhou.
summary.zh: 唐代古文运动领袖，"唐宋八大家"之首，倡导儒学道统、排斥佛老。819年上《论佛骨表》谏迎佛骨，几乎被处死，被贬潮州。

label.en: Demoted to Yangshan for criticising famine relief
Staff officer in the Huaixi campaign against Wu Yuanji
Exiled to Chaozhou after the Buddha-bone memorial
Envoy to the rebel garrison at Zhenzhou
Dies in Chang'an as Vice-Minister of Personnel
label.zh: 卒于长安，官至吏部侍郎

sources.title: 刘昫等《旧唐书》卷160 韩愈传
Britannica: Han Yu
中文维基百科：韩愈

summary.en: Tang calligrapher whose broad, upright regular script became a model for a millennium. As governor of Pingyuan he raised troops against An Lushan; his draft eulogy for a nephew killed in the rebellion is a masterpiece of running script. Sent to negotiate with the rebel Li Xilie, he was killed after refusing to defect.
summary.zh: 唐代书法家，楷书端庄雄伟，世称"颜体"，影响千年。安史之乱时任平原太守，起兵抵抗；为殉难侄子所写的《祭侄文稿》被誉为"天下第二行书"。奉命宣慰叛将李希烈，坚贞不屈，被缢杀。

label.en: Pingyuan: raises troops against An Lushan
label.zh: 平原太守，起兵讨安禄山

label.en: Puzhou: writes the Draft Eulogy for his nephew

Britannica: Yan Zhenqing
National Palace Museum, Taipei: 唐颜真卿祭侄文稿

summary.en: Northern Song official and scholar who supported Wang Anshi's reforms, directed the Bureau of Astronomy, surveyed the Bian canal and led a frontier command against the Xia. His Dream Pool Essays record the magnetic compass needle and declination, Bi Sheng's movable type, fossils and land formation.
summary.zh: 北宋科学家、政治家，支持王安石变法，主持司天监，测量汴渠，曾任鄜延路经略使抵御西夏。所著《梦溪笔谈》记载了指南针与磁偏角、毕昇活字印刷、化石与地貌成因等。

label.en: Directs the Bureau of Astronomy and surveys the Bian canal
Embassy to the Liao court on the border dispute
Commander at Yanzhou against the Western Xia
Disgraced after the fall of Yongle fortress
Retires to the Dream Pool garden at Runzhou
label.zh: 退居润州梦溪园，著《梦溪笔谈》

Nathan Sivin, "Shen Kua", Dictionary of Scientific Biography (1975)

note: The Liao embassy stop is approximate: Shen met the Liao court at its seasonal camp in the Yongan mountains.

summary.en: Northern Song statesman who led the opposition to Wang Anshi's New Policies and spent fifteen years in Luoyang compiling the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, a chronicle of 1,362 years. Recalled as chancellor in 1085, he repealed most of the reforms before dying the next year.
summary.zh: 北宋政治家、史学家，反对王安石变法，退居洛阳十五年，主持编纂编年体通史《资治通鉴》，记事一千三百六十二年。1085年入朝为相，尽废新法，次年去世。

label.en: Born at Guangshan, where his father was magistrate
label.zh: 生于光州光山县（父任县令）

label.en: Presents the first chapters of a general history
label.zh: 进呈《通志》八卷，奉诏续修

label.zh: 退居洛阳独乐园，编修《资治通鉴》

label.en: Chancellor in Kaifeng; dies in office
label.zh: 在开封任宰相，卒于任上

label.en: Buried at his ancestral home, Xia county

summary.en: Southern Song thinker who synthesised Neo-Confucianism into the 'learning of principle', grouped the Four Books and wrote commentaries that became the basis of the civil service examinations from 1313 to 1905. He revived the White Deer Grotto Academy; late in life his teaching was banned as 'false learning'.
summary.zh: 南宋理学集大成者，确立四书体系并作《四书章句集注》，1313年至1905年成为科举考试的标准注本。他复兴白鹿洞书院；晚年遭"庆元党禁"，其学被斥为"伪学"。

label.en: Lin'an: passes the jinshi examination at 19
Goose Lake debate with Lu Jiuyuan
label.zh: 鹅湖之会，与陆九渊论辩

label.en: Nankang: revives the White Deer Grotto Academy
label.zh: 知南康军，复兴白鹿洞书院

label.en: Dies at Kaoting, Jianyang, under the ban

summary.en: Top graduate of 1256, he raised troops when the Mongols advanced, was seized while negotiating with Bayan, escaped and fought on in Jiangxi and Guangdong until captured in 1278. Refusing to serve Kublai, he was executed in Dadu after four years in prison; his Song of the Righteous Spirit became a classic of loyalty.
summary.zh: 1256年状元。元军南下时起兵勤王，出使元营被扣，脱逃后转战江西、广东，1278年兵败被俘。他拒绝忽必烈招降，囚禁四年后在大都就义，所作《正气歌》《过零丁洋》成为忠义名篇。

label.zh: 生于吉州庐陵（今江西吉安）

label.en: Lin'an: first place in the palace examination
Lingding Sea: writes his famous poem; witnesses Yamen
label.zh: 过零丁洋，目睹崖山之败

文天祥《指南录》《正气歌》

summary.en: Yuan scientist who designed new astronomical instruments, including the simplified armilla, ran a network of 27 observing stations and compiled the Shoushi calendar. As a hydraulic engineer he restored canals in Ningxia and built the Tonghui River that brought the Grand Canal into Dadu.
summary.zh: 元代科学家，创制简仪等天文仪器，主持全国二十七处天文观测，编成《授时历》。他还是水利专家，修复西夏旧渠，开凿通惠河，使大运河直通大都。

label.en: Shangdu: presents six water projects to Kublai
Restores the irrigation canals of Ningxia
Dengfeng: builds the Gaocheng observatory tower

中文维基百科：郭守敬

summary.en: Ming physician who spent nearly thirty years writing the Compendium of Materia Medica (Bencao gangmu), describing 1,892 substances with over 11,000 prescriptions, based on reading, travel and his own observation. It was printed in Nanjing in 1593–96 and later translated into many languages.
summary.zh: 明代医药学家，历时近三十年，博览群书、实地考察，著成《本草纲目》，收药1892种、附方一万一千余首。该书1593至1596年间在南京刊刻，后被译成多种文字。

label.en: Wuchang: physician at the Prince of Chu's court
Beijing: briefly at the Imperial Medical Academy
label.zh: 北京：荐入太医院（未久辞归）

label.en: Collects herbs on Mount Wudang and elsewhere
label.zh: 入武当山等地采药考察

Britannica: Li Shizhen
UNESCO Memory of the World: Ben Cao Gang Mu (2011)

note: His service at the Imperial Medical Academy rests on later biographies and is doubted by some scholars.

role.zh: 科学家、政治家、天主教徒

summary.en: Shanghai scholar who met Matteo Ricci, was baptised Paul in 1603, translated the first six books of Euclid with Ricci, promoted sweet potatoes and Western artillery, compiled the Complete Treatise on Agriculture and led the calendar reform with the Jesuits. He rose to Grand Secretary.
summary.zh: 上海人，结识利玛窦，1603年受洗，教名保禄。与利玛窦合译《几何原本》前六卷，推广番薯种植和西洋火器，编著《农政全书》，主持修订《崇祯历书》，官至礼部尚书兼东阁大学士。

label.en: Publishes the Elements of Geometry with Ricci
label.zh: 与利玛窦合译《几何原本》刊行

label.en: Tianjin: experimental farm growing rice in the north
Dies in Beijing; buried at Xujiahui, Shanghai
label.zh: 卒于北京，归葬上海徐家汇

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷251 徐光启传
Britannica: Xu Guangqi
Catherine Jami et al. (eds.), Statecraft and Intellectual Renewal in Late Ming China: The Cross-Cultural Synthesis of Xu Guangqi (2001)

summary.en: Hereditary officer from Dengzhou who recruited and drilled the 'Qi family army' of Zhejiang miners and peasants, defeated the wokou pirates in Zhejiang and Fujian in the 1560s, then for sixteen years commanded the Jizhou frontier north of Beijing, building hollow watchtowers on the Great Wall. He wrote the military manuals Jixiao xinshu and Lianbing shiji.
summary.zh: 登州世袭军官，招募浙江矿工、农民编练"戚家军"，1560年代在浙闽沿海大破倭寇；此后镇守蓟州十六年，在长城上修建空心敌台。著有兵书《纪效新书》《练兵实纪》。

label.en: Zhejiang: recruits the Qi family army at Yiwu
Taizhou: nine victories over the wokou
Fujian: destroys the pirate base at Hengyu
Commander of Jizhou; rebuilds the Great Wall
label.zh: 总理蓟州练兵，修筑敌台

label.en: Transferred to Guangdong after Zhang Juzheng's fall

Britannica: Qi Jiguang
Ray Huang, 1587, A Year of No Significance (1981), ch. 6

role.en: Senior Grand Secretary of the Ming

summary.en: As senior grand secretary for the child Wanli Emperor from 1572, he tightened official accountability, surveyed the land, extended the Single Whip tax reform and refilled the treasury. After his death the emperor stripped his family of honours and property.
summary.zh: 1572年起任万历朝内阁首辅，辅佐幼年万历帝，推行考成法，清丈全国田亩，推广一条鞭法，国库充盈。死后遭万历清算，被抄家夺谥。

label.en: Senior grand secretary for the Wanli Emperor
Returns to Jiangling for his father's burial

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷213 张居正传
Britannica: Zhang Juzheng
中文维基百科：张居正

summary.en: After failing the metropolitan examinations five times, this Jiangxi scholar became a county teacher and wrote The Exploitation of the Works of Nature (Tiangong kaiwu, 1637), an illustrated survey of agriculture, textiles, salt, ceramics, metallurgy, paper and weapons.
summary.zh: 江西学者，五次会试不第，任分宜县教谕时撰成《天工开物》（1637年），图文并茂地记录了农业、纺织、制盐、陶瓷、冶金、造纸、兵器等工艺。

label.en: Prefect of Bozhou; resigns as the Ming falls
label.zh: 任亳州知州，明亡后归隐

sources.title: 宋应星《天工开物》序（崇祯十年）

中文维基百科：宋应星

note: His death date is uncertain (c. 1666).

summary.en: A Jiangyin gentleman who refused the examinations and spent thirty years walking China's mountains and rivers, keeping detailed diaries. His four-year journey through Guangxi, Guizhou and Yunnan (1636–40) produced pioneering descriptions of karst landscapes and identified the Jinsha as the main source of the Yangtze.
summary.zh: 江阴人，不应科举，三十余年遍游名山大川，写下详尽日记。1636至1640年的西南远游历经广西、贵州、云南，对喀斯特地貌作了开创性考察，并指出金沙江是长江正源。

label.en: Mount Tiantai: first entry of his travel diary
label.zh: 天台山：《游天台山日记》开篇

label.en: Tengchong, at the edge of Ming Yunnan
Carried home ill; dies at Jiangyin

sources.title: 徐弘祖《徐霞客游记》
钱谦益《徐霞客传》
Britannica: Xu Hongzu

story.en:
Xu Hongzu, known by his literary name Xiake, 'man of the rosy clouds', came from a wealthy family that had produced scholars for generations. A great-grandfather's involvement in an exam scandal had soured the family on official life, and his mother encouraged him to travel instead, asking only that he go with a purpose and return. For two decades he made trips of a few months each, to Mount Tiantai, Huangshan, the Wuyi hills and the Five Sacred Peaks, writing every evening what he had seen.

After his mother's death he set out in 1636, aged nearly fifty, on the journey of his life. With a monk named Jingwen and a servant he went through Zhejiang and Jiangxi into Hunan, where robbers on the Xiang River took his money; Jingwen later died of illness on the road, and Xu carried his ashes to Jizu Mountain in Yunnan. He crawled into hundreds of limestone caves in Guangxi and measured them, and in Yunnan he followed rivers to argue that the Jinsha, not the Min, was the true upper Yangtze.

By 1640 his legs were paralysed, and Mu Zeng, the Naxi chieftain of Lijiang, had him carried home by litter. He died the next year. His diaries, edited after his death, are a classic of Chinese travel writing and geography.
story.zh:
徐弘祖，号霞客，出身江阴富裕的书香世家。曾祖卷入科场案，家族从此对仕途心灰意冷；母亲鼓励他出游，只嘱咐他"游必有方"，按期归来。二十余年间，他每次外出数月，游天台、黄山、武夷及五岳，每晚记下所见。

母亲去世后，年近五十的徐霞客于1636年开始了平生最远的旅行。他与僧人静闻和一名仆人经浙江、江西入湖南，在湘江遭强盗劫掠；静闻后来病死途中，徐霞客背着他的遗骨一路走到云南鸡足山安葬。他钻入广西数以百计的石灰岩洞穴，逐一测量记录；在云南他追溯江河源流，提出金沙江而非岷江才是长江上源。

到1640年他双足瘫痪，丽江土司派人用滑竿把他送回家乡，次年去世。他死后整理成书的日记，成为中国游记文学和地理学的经典。

summary.en: Grandson of a wealthy Imperial Household bondservant family that held the Jiangning silk commission in Nanjing, he grew up in luxury until the Yongzheng Emperor confiscated the family's property in 1728. Living poor in Beijing's western hills, he wrote Dream of the Red Chamber, left unfinished at his death.
summary.zh: 出身内务府包衣世家，祖父曹寅任江宁织造，幼年在南京享尽富贵。1728年雍正帝抄没曹家，举家迁回北京。晚年在北京西山过着贫困生活，写作《红楼梦》，未竟而卒。

label.en: Born in Nanjing, at the Jiangning Imperial Silk Manufactory
Family property confiscated; moves to Beijing
Lives in the western hills, writing 'The Story of the Stone'
label.zh: 移居西山，"披阅十载，增删五次"

label.en: Manuscript with Red Inkstone commentary circulates
Dies in poverty after the death of his son

sources.title: 《红楼梦》甲戌本脂砚斋评语
Britannica: Cao Zhan
周汝昌《曹雪芹新传》（1992）

note: Both dates are disputed: birth is placed in 1715 or 1724, death in 1763 or 1764 (壬午/癸未除夕). Wikidata gives c. 1710–1765.

role.en: Ming loyalist commander, founder of Tungning
role.zh: 明郑抗清将领、驱荷复台

summary.en: Son of the merchant-admiral Zheng Zhilong and a Japanese mother, he refused to follow his father in surrendering to the Qing and built a maritime army in Fujian. After failing to take Nanjing in 1659, he expelled the Dutch from Taiwan in 1662 and founded the Zheng kingdom of Tungning, but died months later.
summary.zh: 海商郑芝龙之子，母为日本人。父亲降清后，他坚持抗清，在福建沿海建立强大水师。1659年北伐南京失败，1662年驱逐荷兰人收复台湾，建立明郑政权，数月后病逝。

label.en: Studies at the Imperial Academy in Nanjing
Breaks with his father; burns his scholar's robe
Lands at Luermen and besieges Zeelandia
label.zh: 登陆鹿耳门，围攻热兰遮城
荷兰人投降，同年卒于台南

sources.title: Tonio Andrade, Lost Colony: The Untold Story of China's First Great Victory over the West (2011)
Britannica: Koxinga
江日昇《台湾外记》

story.en:
Zheng Sen was born in Hirado to Zheng Zhilong, a pirate turned Ming admiral who controlled the trade of the Taiwan Strait, and a Japanese woman of the Tagawa family. At seven he was brought to his father's fortress at Anhai and given a classical education. When the Ming fell, the Longwu Emperor of the Southern Ming favoured him with the imperial surname Zhu, and he was known ever after as Guoxingye, 'Lord of the Imperial Surname', which Europeans rendered Koxinga.

In 1646 his father went over to the Qing. Koxinga refused, and the Qing army's sack of Anhai led to his mother's death. He is said to have burned his scholar's robes at the Confucian temple and sworn to fight. From Xiamen and Jinmen he built a navy of hundreds of junks financed by overseas trade, and in 1659 he sailed up the Yangtze to besiege Nanjing, only to be routed when he delayed his assault.

Needing a new base, he turned on the Dutch colony on Taiwan. In April 1661 his fleet crossed the shallow channel at Luermen on a high tide. Fort Zeelandia held out for nine months before Governor Frederick Coyett surrendered in February 1662. Koxinga died that June, aged 37; he is honoured on both sides of the strait.
story.zh:
郑森生于日本平户，父亲郑芝龙由海盗转为明朝将领，控制台湾海峡贸易，母亲是日本田川氏。七岁时他被接回父亲在福建安平的据点，接受儒家教育。明亡后，南明隆武帝赐他国姓"朱"，人称"国姓爷"，欧洲人据此称他为Koxinga。

1646年郑芝龙降清。郑成功不肯随父，清军攻掠安平，其母因此身亡。据说他到孔庙焚烧儒服，誓师抗清。他以厦门、金门为基地，凭海外贸易支撑起数百艘战船的水师，1659年溯长江北伐围攻南京，却因迟迟不攻而遭清军反击大败。

为了寻找新的根据地，他把目光投向荷兰人占据的台湾。1661年4月，郑军船队乘涨潮驶过鹿耳门浅水航道。热兰遮城坚守九个月，1662年2月荷兰长官揆一投降。同年6月郑成功病逝，年仅三十七岁；海峡两岸都尊他为民族英雄。

summary.en: A Jianzhou Jurchen chieftain who began his rise in 1583 with, tradition says, thirteen suits of armour, united the Jurchen tribes, created the Eight Banners and a Manchu script, and proclaimed the Later Jin in 1616. He crushed the Ming at Sarhu in 1619 and took Liaodong, but was checked at Ningyuan in 1626 and died that year.
summary.zh: 建州女真首领，相传1583年以"十三副遗甲"起兵，统一女真诸部，创立八旗制度和满文，1616年建立后金。1619年在萨尔浒大败明军，攻占辽东，1626年宁远之战受挫，同年去世。

label.en: Takes up arms to avenge his father and grandfather

label.zh: 在赫图阿拉称汗，建立后金

label.en: Repulsed by Yuan Chonghuan at Ningyuan; dies months later

sources.title: 赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷1 太祖本纪
Britannica: Nurhachi
中文维基百科：努尔哈赤

summary.en: Fourth Qing emperor to rule China, he reigned for sixty years (1735–96) and held real power until his death. His armies destroyed the Dzungars and doubled the empire's territory; he sponsored the Siku quanshu while purging books in a literary inquisition, and in old age let his favourite Heshen plunder the state.
summary.zh: 清朝入关后第四位皇帝，在位六十年（1735–1796），退位后仍以太上皇执政至去世。他平定准噶尔，使疆域大为拓展；编纂《四库全书》，同时大兴文字狱、禁毁书籍；晚年宠信和珅，吏治败坏。

label.en: First of six southern tours, to Hangzhou
Conquest of Dzungaria and the Tarim completed

label.zh: 承德避暑山庄：接见马戛尔尼

label.en: Abdicates but keeps power as Retired Emperor

role.en: Empress dowager and regent of the Qing

summary.en: A Manchu concubine who bore the Xianfeng Emperor's only son, she seized power in 1861 and dominated the court for nearly fifty years as regent for her son Tongzhi and her nephew Guangxu. She ended the Hundred Days' Reform in 1898, backed the Boxers in 1900, then sponsored the late-Qing New Policies.

story.en:
Lady Yehenara entered the Forbidden City in 1852 as a low-ranking concubine. In 1856 she gave the Xianfeng Emperor his only son, and her rank rose. When the emperor fled the Anglo-French advance and died at Chengde in 1861, he left the five-year-old boy under eight regents. Cixi and the senior empress, Ci'an, allied with Prince Gong, arrested the regents on the way back to Beijing, and the two dowagers began to 'listen to government from behind the curtain'.

She ruled for nearly half a century: through the Tongzhi Restoration and the Self-Strengthening Movement, then, after her son died in 1875, as regent for her three-year-old nephew Guangxu. In 1898, when Guangxu's reformers seemed to threaten her, she resumed power and kept him a prisoner. In 1900 she declared war on the foreign powers in support of the Boxers; when the allied armies reached Beijing she fled to Xi'an in peasant dress.

Back in Beijing in 1902 she launched reforms more radical than those she had crushed: modern schools, a new army, the end of the examinations and a plan for a constitution. Guangxu died of arsenic poisoning on 14 November 1908, as tests in 2008 confirmed, and Cixi died the next day.
story.zh:
叶赫那拉氏1852年入宫，封兰贵人。1856年她为咸丰帝生下唯一的皇子载淳，地位随之提高。1861年，避英法联军逃往热河的咸丰帝病死承德，遗命八大臣辅佐五岁的幼帝。慈禧与慈安太后联合恭亲王奕訢，在回京途中拿下顾命大臣，两宫太后从此"垂帘听政"。

她执政近半个世纪：先是同治中兴与洋务运动；1875年同治帝去世后，又立三岁的外甥载湉为光绪帝，继续垂帘。1898年她认为维新派威胁自己，重新训政，把光绪软禁起来。1900年她支持义和团，向列强宣战；八国联军攻入北京，她换上民妇装束仓皇西逃西安。

1902年回到北京后，她推行了比当年扼杀的变法更激进的新政：兴办新式学堂、编练新军、废除科举、筹备立宪。1908年11月14日光绪帝死于砒霜中毒（2008年检测证实），次日慈禧去世。

Mary Backus Rankin, Early Chinese Revolutionaries (1971)
中文维基百科：秋瑾

story.en:
Qiu Jin grew up in an official family, rode horses, practised swordsmanship and wrote poetry, and at twenty was married to the son of a wealthy Hunanese family. In Beijing after the Boxer war she read the reform press and grew restless. In 1904 she sold her jewellery, left her husband and two children, and sailed for Tokyo, where she unbound her feet, sometimes dressed in men's clothes and carried a dagger, and joined Sun Yat-sen's Revolutionary Alliance.

Back in China in 1906 she started the China Women's Journal in Shanghai, calling on women to win their own freedom through education and work. In 1907 she took charge of the Datong school in Shaoxing, which trained young men for a rising planned with her cousin Xu Xilin in Anhui.

Xu Xilin assassinated the governor of Anhui on 6 July 1907 and was executed. Troops surrounded the Datong school on 13 July; Qiu Jin refused to flee and was arrested. Under interrogation she wrote only a single line about autumn wind and autumn rain, punning on her surname. She was beheaded at Xuanting Kou in Shaoxing on 15 July. Four years later the dynasty fell, and Sun Yat-sen wrote an inscription for her tomb by West Lake.
story.zh:
秋瑾出身官宦之家，好骑马击剑，能诗善文，二十岁时嫁给湖南富家子弟王廷钧。庚子之后随夫寓居北京，读到维新报刊，内心日益不安。1904年她变卖首饰，离开丈夫和一对子女东渡日本，放足，时常穿男装、佩短刀，加入孙中山领导的同盟会。

1906年回国后，她在上海创办《中国女报》，号召妇女通过教育和自立争取解放。1907年她主持绍兴大通学堂，以学堂为掩护训练青年，准备与表兄徐锡麟在安徽同时起义。

1907年7月6日，徐锡麟在安庆刺杀安徽巡抚恩铭，事败被杀。7月13日清兵包围大通学堂，秋瑾拒绝出走，被捕。审讯时她只写下"秋风秋雨愁煞人"七字。7月15日她在绍兴轩亭口就义。四年后清朝覆亡，孙中山为她在西湖畔的墓题词。

summary.en: Zhou Shuren of Shaoxing abandoned medicine in Japan to write, and with 'A Madman's Diary' (1918) and 'The True Story of Ah Q' (1921) founded modern Chinese fiction in the vernacular. His biting essays made him the leading voice of the left in his final decade in Shanghai.

story.en:
Lu Xun's grandfather was jailed for bribing an examiner, and his father fell ill and died while the boy carried pawned goods to the pharmacy for useless remedies. He later wrote that he went to Japan to study Western medicine because of those doctors. At Sendai, as he told it in the preface to his first collection, a lecturer showed a lantern slide from the Russo-Japanese War of a Chinese man about to be beheaded as a spy, watched by a crowd of apathetic Chinese. He decided that the nation's spirit, not its bodies, needed curing, and turned to literature.

For years nothing came of it. In 1918, while copying old inscriptions in Beijing, he was asked by a friend for a story for New Youth and wrote 'A Madman's Diary', in which a man reads the Confucian classics and finds the words 'eat people' between the lines. 'The True Story of Ah Q' followed, a portrait of a village loafer who turns every humiliation into a 'spiritual victory'.

In his last decade in Shanghai he wrote mostly short essays, attacking the Nationalist government and quarrelling with fellow leftists, and championed woodcut prints. He died of tuberculosis in 1936.
story.zh:
鲁迅的祖父因科场贿赂案入狱，父亲久病不愈，少年鲁迅常常拿着衣物首饰进当铺，再到药店为父亲抓那些无用的药，父亲终究去世。他后来说，自己赴日学医与这些庸医有关。据他在《呐喊·自序》中所述，在仙台医专的课上，教员放映日俄战争的幻灯片，画面上一个中国人被当作俄国间谍砍头，周围站着一群神情麻木的中国人。他由此认为，要医治的首先是国民的精神，于是弃医从文。

此后多年他一事无成。1918年，正在北京抄古碑的鲁迅应友人钱玄同之约为《新青年》撰稿，写出《狂人日记》：狂人翻开历史，从字缝里看出满本都写着"吃人"两个字。随后的《阿Q正传》塑造了一个把每次屈辱都化为"精神胜利"的乡村流浪汉。

晚年在上海，他主要写杂文，抨击国民政府，也与左翼同人论争，并大力提倡新兴木刻。1936年他因肺结核病逝。
